assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology to GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy is a rare complete arc from hormone discovery and peptide characterization to drugs that reshape treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with growing cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and clinical and societal impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and receptor-mediated actions, translation) and Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form) form a defensible trio. Knudsen (drug design for liraglutide/semaglutide) is a major industrial contributor but the supplied credit allows only three; priority disputes around early GLP-1 work (including Habener's group, who are not in the credited names) remain unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by large outcome trials in several indications; recognition is timely given the scale of clinical use.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among discovery-phase groups, and whether drug development (Knudsen) should displace a discovery laureate.
My recollection of prior major prizes for this work is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells are a new therapeutic modality that produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a platform for cell therapy; the conceptual and clinical impact is large and clear.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design with costimulation and preclinical work), June (first clinical translation and durable responses in CLL/ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, TIL and early gene-engineered T-cell trials) are plausible; Eshhar and others are not in the supplied credit, which leaves the question of foundational CAR priority open.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and multi-year follow-up give strong confirmation; limits in solid tumours and toxicity are evolving but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Foundational priority for the chimeric receptor concept is not fully represented in the credited names.
Whether Rosenberg's contribution is best recognized as part of this discovery or separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity and transformed circuit analysis across systems; the discovery of channelrhodopsins and their use as genetic tools is original, widely adopted and enduring.
assessment.attribution: A fair configuration is hard with six credited names: Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin identification and characterization, with Bamberg), Deisseroth and Boyden (neuronal deployment), Miesenböck (earlier genetic photoactivation concept). I pick the channelrhodopsin discoverers plus the key neuronal implementer, leaving Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck unrecognized, which is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature as a research tool with massive independent adoption; therapeutic translation (e.g., retinal restoration) is early but not required for a physiology prize.
uncertainties: Strict three-person limit excludes several decisive contributors.
Medical relevance is mostly as a tool rather than a treatment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided antisense correction of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, a first effective therapy for a fatal childhood neuromuscular disease, and validated splice-switching oligonucleotides as a therapeutic class.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and identification of the target sequence/ASO strategy) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development) form a clean pair; contributions from other groups (e.g., Singh, Hua, Adrian's collaborators) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with substantial long-term clinical data; the platform extends to other disorders. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize is best framed as a mechanism discovery or a drug development achievement.
Contributions from other labs may be underrepresented.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational inhibition of BCR-ABL with imatinib converted CML from a fatal disease to a chronic one and established the template of targeted cancer therapy, building on identification of the Philadelphia chromosome abnormality and the BCR-ABL fusion.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (compound discovery and project origin) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms, second-generation inhibitors) is a natural trio; earlier foundational work by Rowley, Gray and others lies outside the supplied names, so the credit is for the therapeutic step only.
assessment.maturity: Very mature with two decades of follow-up and independent confirmation; recognition is arguably overdue, which raises a question about how long it has been outstanding.
uncertainties: Foundational cytogenetic and fusion-gene discoveries are not part of this credit.
Chemist contributions (Zimmermann, Matter) fall outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic from ER to nucleus, with IRE1/HAC1 and XBP1 splicing, and links to secretory disease, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently identified key components of the pathway (IRE1 and its target response, HAC1 mRNA splicing); two-person attribution is clean and well-supported.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed across species; disease translation (e.g., ISRIB, UPR modulators) is ongoing and less established, but the basic discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Medical impact is more indirect than for therapeutic candidates.
Contributions of others in the field (Kaufman, Ron) are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunotherapy; the discovery of the second messenger cGAMP is a concise original result.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger) is the central figure; Barber (STING) is the natural second laureate. Others credited (Ishikawa, Sun, Wu) were important contributors but a three-person limit supports Chen and Barber.
assessment.maturity: Basic mechanism is well confirmed; therapeutic agents are still in development, so recognition could be seen as slightly early but the science is firmly established.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is not yet proven.
Attribution between STING and cGAS discoveries involves a possible priority tension.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of BCL11A as a repressor of fetal hemoglobin, derived from human genetics and mechanistic studies, led to clinically effective reactivation of fetal hemoglobin in sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia, a clear bridge from regulatory genetics to cure.
assessment.attribution: Orkin (BCL11A mechanism), Sankaran (genetic association and function) and Bauer (enhancer editing strategy) are the decisive contributors in this credit; Thein's association work on HbF is also substantial, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: First gene-edited therapy approved recently, but long-term follow-up is limited and parts of the story (editing therapy) are very recent, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Short follow-up of the editing therapy.
Allocation between mechanism, genetic association and therapeutic editing is unresolved.
